title: UPDATE: Suspect in Officer Shooting, Waymo Attack Arrested - NewsBreak
text: SANTA MONICA - The suspect who shot and injured a Santa Monica police officer near the Santa Monica Place Mall on Wednesday has been arrested and confirmed as the same individual wanted in connection with Sunday's shooting of two juveniles in a driverless Waymo vehicle, authorities said. Santa Monica police issued an alert around 1:30 p.m. urging the public to avoid the area near Fourth Street and Colorado Avenue, where the officer was wounded during an exchange with the suspect. The officer was transported to a hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, according to Mayor Lana Negrete. Law enforcement from Santa Monica, Los Angeles, and El Segundo, along with K-9 units, conducted a coordinated search. The immediate area was cleared by 2:30 p.m., but an active search continued through the afternoon until the suspect was taken into custody. "The suspect involved in today's shooting of an SMPD officer has been arrested," the department announced in a late-day update. "He has also been confirmed as the individual wanted in connection with the recent Waymo vehicle shooting." That earlier incident occurred Sunday night near Second Street and Broadway, where police say the suspect opened fire on an autonomous Waymo vehicle following a verbal altercation with the juveniles inside. Both teens were injured. A photo of the suspect had been circulated publicly earlier in the day. His name has not yet been released. "We're grateful for the support of our regional partners and the community during this investigation," the Santa Monica Police Department said. Councilmember Lana Negrete addressed public concern during the lockdown, particularly from parents of students and summer camp attendees. "Please practice caution by staying indoors and avoiding downtown," she said earlier. "We're working with all partners to ensure the safety of schools, parks, businesses, and anyone in the area."
